title: Concrete Steps by ASEAN to Facilitate Return to Stability in Myanmar
what_it_is: Concrete Steps by ASEAN to Facilitate Return to Stability in Myanmar

sections.label: Myanmar violence and Rohingya aid
sections.summary: Questions ask what ASEAN will do about Myanmar violence and whether Singapore will send more Rohingya aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs given the escalating developments in Myanmar involving the use of violence by security forces against demonstrators such as the violence seen in Mandalay on 20 February 2021 (a) what concrete steps will ASEAN take to facilitate a return to stability in Myanmar; and (b) what are the immediate and long-term consequences for the region if the situation does not abate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs whether Singapore will consider sending another consignment of humanitarian aid to the Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazaar, Bangladesh, since the efforts to repatriate the Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar have stalled.

sections.label: UN reported deaths
sections.summary: The United Nations reported that 38 people died on 3 March alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The United Nations reported that on 3 March alone, 38 people died.

sections.label: ASEAN ministers urge restraint
sections.summary: ASEAN Foreign Ministers urged Myanmar's military to exercise utmost restraint and refrain from lethal force against unarmed civilians.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The ASEAN Foreign Ministers urged the Myanmar military authorities to exercise the utmost restraint and to refrain from the use of lethal force against unarmed civilians.

sections.label: Singapore humanitarian aid contributions
sections.summary: Singapore has contributed over S$1 million in bilateral humanitarian aid to Bangladesh and Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore has contributed over S$1 million in bilateral humanitarian aid to both Bangladesh and Myanmar.

sections.label: Myanmar democratic transition and reconciliation
sections.summary: Singapore and ASEAN hope Myanmar succeeds in democratic transition and national reconciliation, but only Myanmar's people can find a sustainable political solution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore and ASEAN hope that Myanmar will succeed in its path towards democratic transition and national reconciliation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will do what we can to support this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But, ultimately, only the people of Myanmar, including Tatmadaw, the NLD, and the diverse ethnic groups, some of whom have armed militias, only they can find a sustainable political solution that is in the best interest of their people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We can only hope that wisdom will prevail.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And despite all the bloodshed so far, I still think it is not too late.

sections.label: Foreign ministers daily contact
sections.summary: The short answer is yes and the foreign ministers are in daily contact with one another.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The short answer is yes and the foreign ministers are in daily contact with one another.

sections.label: Myanmar military and sanctions
sections.summary: Myanmar's military has not responded to economic sanctions, moral opprobrium or ASEAN Charter human rights references over 70 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Again, if you look over the past 70 years, the military authorities in Myanmar frankly do not respond to economic sanctions, do not respond to moral opprobrium.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And certainly, references to the ASEAN Charter in Human Rights, whilst essential, are not sufficient to change their behaviour.

sections.label: Keys lie within Myanmar
sections.summary: Singaporeans should not raise false hopes or incite violence, as reconciliation ultimately lies within Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Do not raise false hopes, do not incite and do not encourage further crystallisation of disputes and violence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I say all this so that Singaporeans, both within this House and outside this House, will understand that despite all our fervent and earnest hopes of reconciliation, the keys ultimately lie within Myanmar.
